blocks.heading: Calculating cost-plus and promotional prices
blocks.text: For cost-plus pricing, calculate the mark-up on the stated cost and add it to that cost. A mark-up on cost is different from a profit margin on sales. For a promotional percentage reduction, calculate the reduction on the original selling price and subtract it. State the base, currency and final price. A discount on a cost-plus price is applied to the resulting selling price, not silently to the original cost. The final price must still be assessed against demand and relevant costs; arithmetic alone does not establish a good strategy.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Luma Cases has full unit cost N$80 and applies a 25% mark-up on cost, then offers 10% off that selling price. Mark-up = 80 × 0.25 = N$20. Normal price = 80 + 20 = N$100. Reduction = 100 × 0.10 = N$10. Promotional price = 100 − 10 = N$90. The final price leaves N$10 above the stated unit cost, before any new cost not included in it.

blocks.heading: Calculating a cost-plus price
blocks.text: Multiply the stated unit cost by the mark-up rate as a decimal to find the added amount, then add it to cost. Check whether the rate is a mark-up on cost rather than a margin on revenue. State the final selling price in N$ and retain appropriate cents. The price provides a surplus over the included cost only if customers buy at that price.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Tano Packs has full unit cost N$120 and a 20% mark-up on cost. Mark-up = 120 × 0.20 = N$24. Price = 120 + 24 = N$144. The added N$24 is 20% of cost, not 20% of the final selling price.

blocks.heading: Calculating a promotional price
blocks.text: For a percentage discount, multiply the original price by the discount rate, then subtract that reduction from the original price. The base is the price being discounted. A 15% reduction leaves 85% of the original price, not 15%. State both the reduction and final price clearly so customers’ saving is not confused with the amount payable.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Eha Bags reduces an original N$150 price by 15%. Discount = 150 × 0.15 = N$22.50. Promotional price = 150 − 22.50 = N$127.50. Customers save N$22.50, not N$127.50.
